npc_steward.title: Steward Wren Ashby
lines: "I was polishing silver in the cellar all evening," he insists, hands trembling.
"I wasn't doing nothing in the Barn, so if you saw me over there it wasn't me!"

npc_voss.title: Commodore Brannigan Voss
lines: "I heard the toast from the watch post," Voss says, a little too quickly.
"Ask anyone. I've nothing to hide." He stares at you intently as he says this.

npc_kestrel.title: Merchant Odalys Kestrel
lines: "I never even spoke to Lord Duskmere tonight," Kestrel claims, arms folded.
"I was working all evening until they called us over here. Go on and check the dock office if you don't believe me."

npc_marrow.title: Architect Tobias Marrow
lines: "I was proud to have played my part in rebuilding these walls," Marrow says, gesturing at the estate house.
"Every stone on schedule, a-and to the letter of the contract." He doesn't quite meet your eyes when he says it.

npc_ashgate.title: Lady Isobel Ashgate
lines: She regards you coolly over the rim of her glass, entirely unbothered by the commotion.

"A dreadful business. Alaric and I had our disagreements, of course, land mostly, tedious inheritance laws, but murder? I have people for that sort of thing. I certainly don't attend to it myself." She smiles, and gives you absolutely nothing else.

npc_corwin.title: Silas "Hook" Corwin
lines: He looks you up and down, then leans in close.
"You lot look like you're about to get blamed for somethin' you didn't do. "
"If you want to know more about Marrow, he's left a survey marker out near the river. Always thought that was odd."

npc_nell.title: Nell Cobb
lines: "Didn't expect to see Champions of Azeroth at a fancy garden party!"
"Free drinks though, can't complain. Shame about the whole murder-death-thing. Really put a damper on the evening." she slurs.
"Between us? I saw the Commodore down by the river a few nights back. Didn't think much of it at the time, but now murder? Suspect if you ask me."

npc_reyes.title: Sergeant Reyes
lines: The watch sergeant won't quite meet your eyes. "I was on my rounds. The whole time. "
He keeps glancing over the bridge and looking back towards the manor.

npc_maid.title: A Lady's Maid
lines: She's pacing around near the farm animals, doing her best not to look nervous.
"I've been working the whole evening, sir. I swear. I haven't gone nowhere." Her hands are shaking, and she keeps glancing toward the farm animals.
Then again, maybe she just doesn't like cows?

npc_guest_a1.title: A Gala Guest
lines: "Terrible thing, isn't it? Though between us, Duskmere's wine cellar is still the best. Shame to let it go to waste tonight."

npc_guest_a2.title: A Gala Guest
lines: "I heard the Commodore wanted this whole gala moved up a week. Odd, that. Probably nothing."

npc_guest_a3.title: A Gala Guest
lines: "Surprised to see Lady Ashgate still here - I heard the engagement was called off awfully suddenly..."

doc_ashby.title: The Repair Ledger
doc_ashby.intro: A ledger of several repair-fund withdrawals sits beside a small stack of numbered receipt stubs.
list: Stub 401, Coastwood Timber, 40,000g
Stub 402, Coastwood Timber, 25,000g
Stub 403, Ironbell Smithy, 15,000g
Stub 404, Harrow & Vale, 90,000g
Stub 405, Coastwood Timber, 55,000g
Stub 406, Ironbell Smithy, 20,000g
doc_ashby.closing: Six stubs for seven withdrawals. If they were issued in ledger order, simply skipping whichever entry lacked a receipt, stub 404 ought to belong to the fifth withdrawal, the Coastwood Timber roof beams. Instead it's stamped for Harrow & Vale, the seventh. Something's been renumbered to cover a gap. The 14th withdrawal, paid straight to 'Duskmere Estate' itself for a contingency reserve, has no stub at all.

doc_voss.title: The Burnt Satchel
doc_voss.intro: Half-buried, a satchel holds five torn, part-burned betting slips. None show a full date, only fragments of context.
list: "...paid in full after the regatta on the 2nd, no hard feelings, B.V." (5,000g)
"...third marker this month, Voss, I'm done extending you credit" (20,000g)
"...since the Siege repairs started, you've been good for it, but this one's steep" (35,000g)
"...if this isn't settled by the gala tomorrow I'm bringing it to Thorne myself" (80,000g)
"...he swears the ship's coming in any day now. It never does." (a side note, different hand, no amount)
doc_voss.closing: The regatta came before the Siege repairs began. Read in that order, the debt only grows, and the largest, most recent slip threatens to go straight to Thorne by tomorrow night.

doc_kestrel.title: The Shipping Manifests
doc_kestrel.intro: A dock office, and inside, a stack of shipping manifests.
doc_kestrel.closing: Two of these describe the same ship, Providence's Grace, departing and arriving in the same instant, twice. No ship sails that fast. Something was filed on paper that never needed to happen on water.

doc_marrow.title: The Blueprint Tube
doc_marrow.intro: Buried near the survey marker, a tube holding two documents: the original contracted repairs, and a second sheet recording what actually got built.
doc_marrow.closing: Two structures exist on the grounds that never appeared on the original contract. Marrow built them anyway, and was never paid for the overage.

doc_ashgate.title: Torn Paperwork
doc_ashgate.intro: A chest holds a letter torn into six pieces, mixed in with a receipt and a dinner invitation that don't seem to matter at all.
list: "...the anniversary of the Siege. I cannot say this..."
"...cover the debts by autumn. If the engagement proceeds as..."
"...to anyone, least of all him, until it is settled..."
"...the solicitor confirms House Ashgate's holdings will not..."
"...paperwork can be finalized within the month, well before..."
"...planned, everything changes. I am told the..."
doc_ashgate.closing: Pieced together in order, the letter reads: 'The solicitor confirms House Ashgate's holdings will not cover the debts by autumn. If the engagement proceeds as planned, everything changes. I am told the paperwork can be finalized within the month, well before the anniversary of the Siege. I cannot say this to anyone, least of all him, until it is settled.' Weeks before the gala, and already a matter of real urgency.

doc_reyes.title: The Patrol Rota
doc_reyes.intro: Folded inside a broken lantern near the bridge: a watch schedule, in City Watch bells rather than plain hours.
list: First Bell, dusk
Second Bell, one candle-mark after dusk
Third Bell, two candle-marks after dusk
Fourth Bell, midnight
Fifth Bell, two candle-marks after midnight
doc_reyes.closing: A second note is stapled to the top, half-torn: 'R. asked to swap Third for Fourth, said he'd cover the gap himself, told no one.' A crossed-out watch log shows someone else covering Fourth Bell instead. Reyes' actual post, Third Bell, two candle-marks after dusk, was empty.

doc_maid.title: The Hidden Diary
doc_maid.intro: Buried beneath a loose stone: a diary, half in plain hand, half in a simple lover's code.
list: "He held my hand under the table at supper and I nearly dropped the whole tray. I don't think anyone saw. I hope no one saw."
"I know how it looks, a maid and a Watchman. I don't care anymore. Let them look."
"He says he could lose his post over this, if the wrong person noticed. I told him I didn't care about that either. That part's a lie. I care very much."

(decoded) "He waits for me where the old boathouse used to stand, past the willow, where no one from the house ever walks after dark. Same as every night the bells fall quiet, R. always knows when it's safe."
"If anyone ever finds this diary I will simply die. Burying it deeper tonight."
doc_maid.closing: Whoever she's meeting, she's gone to real trouble to avoid naming him outright, except for one slip. 'The bells fall quiet' and the initial 'R.' both point somewhere specific, if you know where else to look.

evidence_table.title: The Evidence Table
evidence_table.description: Bring every piece of evidence you're carrying and add it to the table.

notebook_page_1.title: A Second Loose Page
notebook_page_1.intro: A scrap of paper, covered in... drawings of food? 🍩🍊 🍜🍊🍅 🥚🍎🍅 🍅🌭🥚 🍓🍅🥚🍉. Maybe it's just from a hungry guard?
notebook_page_1.closing: You fold it back up. If it means anything, it isn't obvious.

notebook_page_2.title: A Loose Page
notebook_page_2.intro: In a cramped scrawl, you can vaguely make out the letters: WKH NHB LV QRW KHUH. The rest of the paper is blank.
notebook_page_2.closing: A shifted alphabet, maybe. Or someone's idea of a joke.

notebook_page_3.title: Another Loose Page
notebook_page_3.intro: A single line, underlined twice like it mattered to someone: DILMT ILLN
notebook_page_3.closing: Someone wanted this to look important. That's not the same thing.

area2_chest_1.title: A Chest
area2_chest_1.intro:
Tucked under the false lid, a strip of paper with a string of numbers:

6-1-11-5   7-15-12-4

No key, no explanation -- just the numbers, and whatever they're worth.
area2_chest_1.closing: Numbers for letters, probably. Doesn't change what's actually in the chest: nothing.

area2_chest_2.title: An Unlocked Chest
area2_chest_2.intro: There's nothing exciting inside - just cobwebs, dust and a scrap of paper with drawings on it: 🍜🍊 🍇🍊🍋🍩 🌭🥚🍙🥚. No wonder it wasn't locked.
area2_chest_2.closing: Same code as the page upstairs. Still no idea what it says.

door_area4_lower_stores.successText: The key turns. The Lower Stores door swings open.
door_area4_lower_stores.lockedText: Locked. The Quartermaster's note said something about not hiding valuables with valuables -- maybe the key is hidden somewhere unassuming.

area4_hidden_key.firstText: You dig through the crate -- straw packing, an old rope, nothing else. Worth a second look, maybe.
area4_hidden_key.foundText: Wedged into a gap under the straw, out of sight unless you already knew to check: a small brass key.

area4_chest.lockedText: Locked. Small keyhole -- whatever opens it, it isn't going to be forced.
area4_chest.foundText: The little brass key turns. Inside, half-buried in straw: a heavier iron key.

npc_blacksmith_surface.title: The Blacksmith
lines:
"Kestrel? Sure, know her. Buys nails and hinges same as anyone shipping crates." He does not look up from the anvil, engrossed in his work.

"A receipt with her name on it? Could be, I do a lot of paperwork." He shrugs, hammer never breaking rhythm.

"Nothing more to say about it than that."

npc_blacksmith_reveal.title: The Blacksmith
lines:
He sets the hammer down this time. "Alright. A receipt with her name on it, dated the night of the gala? Could be." A pause.

"Could also be dated a few days off."

"Wouldn't be the first favor I've done for a regular customer who needed paperwork to say something convenient."

"Nothing to do with any murder, if that's what you're fishing for. Just a woman trying to look like she was somewhere she wasn't, for reasons that are her business, not mine."

npc_head_warlock.title: The Head Warlock
lines: He doesn't look up from the pentagram chalked into the floor. "Champions of Azeroth. In the tower. Joy. How thrilling for me." He continues to stare ahead, not looking at you. "I know why you're here. I know most things that happen in this town, whether I want to or not." He still doesn't look up. "Doesn't mean any of them are worth saying out loud."

npc_head_mage.title: The Head Mage
lines: He gestures vaguely at the window, not breaking his line of sight from whatever he's scrying. "I take it you want gossip, not magic." He sighs. "Fine." "The night of the gala, I had this window open for the stars. The forge over the way never lit. Not once, all night. Odd, for a man who works metal for a living." A thin smile stretches across his face. "Make of that what you will." He winks.

boardClues.title: The empty chair
boardClues.text: The fighter lowers his shield half an inch. "You're not here about the dice game, are you?" A beat. "No? Shame. That empty chair's still bothering half the barracks."

boardClues.title: Gone mid-game
boardClues.text: "Commodore Voss? Used to sit in on our dice nights, regular as anything," the fighter says, not looking up from the mannequin. "That night, he vanished mid-game. Chair sat empty the better part of an hour. Nobody's said where he got to."

boardClues.title: Ash and roses
boardClues.text: The stone dragon's jaw does not move, but the words come anyway, low as a bellows drawing breath. "Ash and roses smell the same to the dead. The tower's own fire burns only for those it favors. A cold hearth, on the night it should have roared, tells truer tales than any warm one ever will."

boardClues.title: The forge never lit
boardClues.text: "The night of the gala, I had this window open for the stars. The forge below never lit. Not once, all night. Odd, for a man who works metal for a living."

boardClues.title: Just paperwork
boardClues.text: "A receipt with her name on it? Could be, I do a lot of paperwork." He shrugs, hammer never breaking rhythm. "Nothing more to say about it than that."

boardClues.title: A backdated favor
boardClues.text: "Wouldn't be the first favor I've done for a regular customer who needed paperwork to say something convenient." Nothing to do with any murder, just a woman trying to look like she was somewhere she wasn't.
boardClues.source: The Blacksmith, Training Ground (after learning the forge never lit)

boardClues.title: Going through his ledgers
boardClues.text: "Sat right over there most of the evening, going through his own ledgers, muttering about materials. Practically lived at that stall."

boardClues.title: Shuttered early
boardClues.text: "We all shuttered early that night. Boarded up well before dusk, ahead of the gala procession. Nobody was doing business out here after that."

boardClues.title: Not here at all that night
boardClues.text: "That ledger business was that morning, not the night of the gala." That evening, Marrow was seen heading back toward the Estate, to the east wall scaffolding.
boardClues.source: The Armour Seller, Market (after hearing the stalls were shuttered early)

boardClues.title: A very specific vial
boardClues.text: The glassblower recalls an odd customer commissioning a very small, tightly-sealable vial, unusually specific about size and discretion.

boardClues.title: Would it show through wine
boardClues.text: She came back a second time, more insistent, asking whether the vial's contents would show through wine once poured, and whether a given tint would still read against red wine specifically.
boardClues.source: The Glassmaker, Glass Workshop (after hearing she seemed anxious)

boardClues.title: Drinking all night
boardClues.text: "Solid as anyone I've poured for," the bartender says. "He was right there at the end of the bar, from before sundown 'til well past the bell."

boardClues.title: A second, higher-stakes game
boardClues.text: "He did slip out for a stretch. Long enough his drink went flat." A rougher game upstairs, by her guess. Not murder. Just a man who welched and didn't want to explain it.
boardClues.source: The Bartender, Inn (after hearing about the empty chair)

boardClues.title: Seemed anxious
boardClues.text: "Odd all evening," the gala guest says. "Kept drifting back to the drinks table like she'd lost something there. Wouldn't sit still, wouldn't finish a conversation."

boardClues.title: Buried in paperwork
boardClues.text: "Buried in paperwork the whole night. Kept muttering about the books not adding up. Didn't have it in him to plan a murder, if you ask me."

boardClues.title: Wouldn't share a drop
boardClues.text: "That's exactly what she wouldn't let me near. Kept it right by her, poured from it herself and everything." A drunk goblin, connecting dots he didn't know he had.
boardClues.source: A Cheering Goblin, the Inn (after hearing about the vial question)

boardClues.title: A confession during matins
boardClues.text: "I heard her confession myself, during matins. Long before the gala ever began, of course."

boardClues.title: Penance before sundown
boardClues.text: "The Commodore? Left before sundown, actually, here for a private penance."

boardClues.title: Sneaking in at midnight
boardClues.text: "I saw the architect myself, sneaking through the servants' entrance, well past midnight."

boardClues.title: At evening prayers
boardClues.text: "Lady Ashgate was here the whole evening. Evening prayers, same as always. I'd stake my own name on it."

boardClues.title: Nobles, eh
boardClues.text: "Wouldn't share a drop of whatever she had, all night. Practically hissed at me when I reached for it." Sounds like nothing. At the time, it was nothing.

boardClues.title: Lighting candles all week
boardClues.text: "The Steward's been in every day this week. Lighting candles. A lot of them." A pause. "Man like that doesn't pray for nothing."

boardClues.title: Fidgeting with her gloves
boardClues.text: "There was a woman in not long back, wouldn't stop fidgeting with her gloves the whole time he worked. Never seen someone so nervous over a little glass vial."

npc_priest.title: The Priest
lines: He barely glances up from the altar. "Whatever you need, I am sure it can wait. Or find someone else. I am, as you can see, thoroughly occupied."

npc_chapel_parishioner.title: A Parishioner
lines: "Terrible business at the Estate," they murmur, eyes still on the altar. "Terrible. We pray for the family."

npc_glassblower_surface.title: The Glassmaker
lines:
He doesn't look up from the pipe he's turning over the flame. "A vial? Sure, I make plenty. Small, sealed tight, easy to carry without it rattling."

"Had someone in not long ago wanting exactly that. Didn't think much of it. People want discreet vials for all sorts of reasons, perfume, medicine, ink."

npc_glassblower_reveal.title: The Glassmaker
lines:
He sets the pipe down properly this time. "Funny you ask. She came back a second time, more insistent. Wanted to know if whatever went in the vial would show through wine once it was poured."

"Asked me straight out whether a certain tint would still read against red wine. I make glass, not poison, so I told her I couldn't say for certain. She didn't seem to like that answer."

He shrugs. "Strange thing to need glass for. Strange thing to ask a glassblower at all, now that I think on it."

npc_shopkeeper_glass.title: The Shopkeeper
lines:
"Looking for glassware? The master's through the back, past the archway. I just mind the counter."

"Actually, funny you ask about customers. There was a woman in not long back, wouldn't stop fidgeting with her gloves the whole time he worked. Never seen someone so nervous over a little glass vial."

npc_monk_impossible.title: A Monk
lines:
He greets you warmly, glad of the company. "Terrible business at the Estate. I hope it's all sorted soon."

"I heard her confession myself, during matins. Long before the gala ever began, of course."

npc_monk_voss.title: A Monk
lines:
"The Commodore? I remember him well. Left before sundown, actually, here for a private penance."

"Gambling debts, I'd guess, though it isn't my place to ask."

npc_monk_marrow.title: A Monk
lines:
"The architect, you mean? I saw him myself, sneaking through the servants' entrance, well past midnight."

"Furtive sort of thing. I did wonder what he had to hide."

npc_monk_ashgate.title: A Monk
lines:
"Lady Ashgate? She was here the whole evening. Evening prayers, same as always."

"I'd stake my own name on it."

npc_bartender_tavern_surface.title: The Bartender
lines:
"Commodore Voss? Regular enough face in here." He keeps wiping the same spot on the bar. "Gala night he was parked right there at the end, drinking steady, from before sundown 'til well past the bell. Solid as anyone I've poured for."

"Don't know what you're after, but if you're asking whether he left, the answer's no. I'd have noticed. He tips well and complains worse, hard to miss either one."

npc_bartender_tavern_reveal.title: The Bartender
lines:
He glances up properly this time. "Empty chair, you said? Ah. All right. Between us, he did slip out for a stretch. Not the whole night, mind, just long enough that I noticed the same drink sitting flat when he came back."

"Went to a second game, is my guess. A rougher one. Upstairs. He came back looking like a man who'd rather not explain himself, which is usually about welching, not murder. Draw your own conclusions."

npc_gossip_guest.title: A Gala Guest, Deep in Her Cups
lines:
She leans in like she's been waiting all night for someone to ask. "Lady Ashgate? Odd all evening, if you want my honest word on it. Kept drifting back to the drinks table like she'd lost something there."

"Wouldn't sit still, wouldn't finish a conversation. My husband said I was imagining it. I wasn't imagining it."

npc_ashby_witness.title: A Weary-Looking Guest
lines:
"The Steward? Buried in paperwork the whole night, far as I saw. Practically had to shout to get a word out of him."

"Kept muttering about the books not adding up. Poor man looked like he hadn't slept in a week." "Didn't have it in him to *plan* a murder, if you ask me, let alone pull one off."

npc_parishioner_ashby_whisper.title: A Parishioner
lines: She doesn't look at you, keeps her eyes on the altar. "The Steward's been in every day this week," she says, barely above a breath. "Lighting candles. A lot of them." A pause. "Man like that doesn't pray for nothing."

npc_goblin_tavern_surface.title: A Cheering Goblin
lines: "Lady Ashgate? Hah! Wouldn't share a drop of whatever she had, all night. Practically hissed at me when I reached for it." He laughs it off, sloshing his mug. "Nobles, eh. Probably wasn't even good wine."

npc_goblin_tavern_reveal.title: A Cheering Goblin
lines: He squints at you, the joke suddenly less funny. "Wait. A little glass vial, you said?" He goes quiet for a goblin. "That's, hah, that's exactly what she wouldn't let me near. Kept it right by her, poured from it herself and everything. Didn't think nothing of it at the time."

vote_clear_ashby.speaker: Silas "Hook" Corwin
lines:
Corwin shakes his head before you've even finished.  "Ashby? The man's been lighting candles and drowning himself in ledgers since the night it happened. That's not a murderer's guilt, that's an accountant who knows an audit's coming."

"Forgery's a hanging offence on its own, no need to hang poison on him too. He's not your man."

vote_clear_voss.speaker: Silas "Hook" Corwin
lines:
"Voss vanished from that dice game for the better part of an hour, sure," Corwin says, "but I know exactly where he really was, and it isn't anywhere near a goblet of wine."

"Man welched on a second, rougher game and couldn't face the table after. That's shameful. It isn't murder."

vote_clear_kestrel.speaker: Silas "Hook" Corwin
lines:
"Kestrel's receipt was backdated, I'll give you that," Corwin says, "but that's the blacksmith covering something else entirely, not her. The forge sat cold and dark the whole night, an apprentice up at the tower saw it herself."

"She was nowhere near the gala when it mattered. Whatever she's hiding, it isn't this."

vote_clear_marrow.speaker: Silas "Hook" Corwin
lines:
"Marrow lied about where he was that evening, no question," Corwin admits, "but not to cover poison. He was back at the Estate's east wall scaffolding, in plain sight, going over materials he was never paid for."

"A man circling what he's owed isn't hiding a murder. He's just embarrassed about being broke."

vote_tie.speaker: Silas "Hook" Corwin
lines: Corwin looks between the split picks and folds his arms. "You can't name two murderers and call it a night. Talk it through properly this time, and vote again."

vote_correct.speaker: Silas "Hook" Corwin
lines:
Corwin goes quiet for a long moment, then nods slowly. "Ashgate. Alright. That tracks with everything else we've got."

"We're not done yet, though. Knowing who isn't the same as proving how. Let's go find out what was actually in that goblet."

npc_armour_seller_market_surface.title: The Armour Seller
lines: "Marrow? The architect fella, yeah? Sat right over there most of the night," he says, nodding toward an empty table across the square. "Going through 'is ledgers, muttering about materials." "Practically lived there for a few hours."

npc_armour_seller_market_reveal.title: The Armour Seller
lines:
He rubs the back of his neck. "Shuttered that early, you said? Huh. Now that you mention it, that ledger business was that morning, not the night of the gala. My memory ain't what it used to be."

"That evening he wasn't here at all. I did see him heading back toward the Estate, though." "Think it was near the east wall, where the scaffolding still is by the ol' temple. Didn't think much of it at the time."

npc_bread_seller_market.title: The Bread Seller
lines: "Everything's fresh," she says, then pauses. "Funny thing, we all shuttered early that night. Boarded up well before dusk, ahead of the gala. Nobody was doing business out here after that."
